- \(p(1)\): \((2\,3)\) fixes \(1\), then \((1\,2\,5\,4)\) sends \(1\mapsto 2\), so \(p(1)=2\).
- \(p(2)\): \((2\,3)\) sends \(2\mapsto 3\), then \((1\,2\,5\,4)\) fixes \(3\), so \(p(2)=3\).
- \(p(3)\): \((2\,3)\) sends \(3\mapsto 2\), then \((1\,2\,5\,4)\) sends \(2\mapsto 5\), so \(p(3)=5\).
- \(p(5)\): \((2\,3)\) fixes \(5\), then \((1\,2\,5\,4)\) sends \(5\mapsto 4\), so \(p(5)=4\).
- \(p(4)\): \((2\,3)\) fixes \(4\), then \((1\,2\,5\,4)\) sends \(4\mapsto 1\), so \(p(4)=1\).

Thus \(p=(1\,2\,3\,5\,4)\), a 5-cycle. The order of a 5-cycle is \(5\), so \(|\langle p\rangle|=5\). Since \(|S_5|=5!=120\), the index is

\[

[S_5:\langle p\rangle]=\frac{|S_5|}{|\langle p\rangle|}=\frac{120}{5}=24.

\]
